notes: Built from the single clean copy in the PDF (no redline). Dates: Original Effective Date 04/27/00 (effective_date), Reviewed 04/24/25 (reviewed_date), Revised 05/15/25.

Code-to-pathway mapping: the code table is not tied to sections, so codes were mapped by their CPT descriptors. 15820/15821 (lower eyelid blepharoplasty) -> lower_eyelid_blepharoplasty; 15822/15823 (upper eyelid blepharoplasty) -> upper_eyelid_blepharoplasty; 67901-67908 (repair of blepharoptosis) -> blepharoptosis_repair; 67900 (repair of brow ptosis) -> brow_lift. The opening position statement names all three procedure families, so restore_function_general lists every code explicitly (rather than an empty list) so that it is checked alongside the specific pathway for each code.

Judgment call: the opening statement 'meet the definition of medical necessity when the goal of the surgery is to restore function to a structure that has been altered by trauma, infection, inflammation, degeneration, neoplasia, or developmental errors (e.g., congenital ptosis)' uses the document's coverage formula, so it is built as its own pathway (restore_function_general). A reviewer could instead read it as an introductory principle with the procedure-specific sections as the only operative criteria; if so, drop that pathway. It does add coverage the specific sections lack (e.g., lower-lid reconstruction after trauma or tumor, congenital ptosis).

The phrases 'to correct obstruction of central vision' (upper blepharoplasty) and 'to relieve obstruction of central vision' (blepharoptosis repair) are treated as the purpose of the section, not as separate criteria: the listed indications (dermatitis, anophthalmic socket prosthesis, thyroid sequelae, nerve palsy, trauma) do not each involve central-vision obstruction, and the vision/visual-field criteria carry the requirement where it applies.

Upper blepharoplasty dermatitis bullet split into three criteria: the condition, 'unresponsive to conservative therapy', and the documentation sentence (onset, prior treatment, extent, discharge, color). A chart can show the condition without the failed therapy or the documentation.

Prosthesis difficulties, thyroid sequelae and nerve palsy each carry 'which must be described and include a history of the present treatment'; built as condition AND a documentation criterion. The three documentation criteria have identical verbatim text (the PDF repeats it) and distinct ids/questions.
'Accidental injury, trauma, or congenital defect' has no documentation clause in the PDF and is a single leaf.

The *NOTE after the Brow Lift section ('If visual field testing is not completed as indicated above, the medical documentation must support evidence of the medical condition which prevents the performance of the test') waives visual field testing. It is applied as an any() around the visual field block in upper_eyelid_blepharoplasty and in blepharoptosis_repair (the two sections that require visual field testing). The brow lift section has no visual field test requirement, so the NOTE does not touch it. The examples (severe tremors, macular degeneration, physical deformities, glaucoma) are illustrative ('may include'), not an exhaustive list. The same waiver criterion is shared by both pathways. The NOTE waives only the visual field testing; photographs are still required.

Visual field thresholds: before taping superior visual field <= 20 degrees; after taping increase >= 30%. The upper blepharoplasty and blepharoptosis sections word these differently, so each section has its own verbatim criteria with the same thresholds.
MRD criterion: '≤ to 2 mm' kept verbatim (the PDF uses the ≤ glyph); threshold lte 2 mm. Definitions section says MRD-1 refers to the upper eyelid margin.

Lower eyelid blepharoplasty sentence split into the symptom ('corneal and/or conjunctival injury, irritation, tearing or pain') and the cause ('due to ectropion, entropion or trichiasis'); both are required.

Brow lift first bullet split into 'Brow ptosis is causing a functional impairment of upper/outer visual fields' and 'documented complaints of interference with vision or visual field related activities ...'; the document's 'BOTH' therefore becomes an all() of three leaves (impairment, complaints, photographs). The parenthetical '(i.e., repair of brow ptosis due to laxity of the forehead muscles)' is descriptive and not a criterion.

Exclusions: each of the three procedure sections has the same two 'does not meet the definition of medical necessity when performed' bullets. Built as six exclusions (two bullets x three sections), each tied to that section's codes; the bullet text is identical across sections. The verbatim text stays inside each bullet because the PDF's bullet glyph separates the sentence stem from the bullet.

Left out: the DESCRIPTION section (background); the LOINC sentence 'The following information may be required documentation to support medical necessity ...' and the LOINC table's 'six months or fewer before starting date of service' time frame (advisory 'may be required', not a coverage criterion); the Definitions section; the step therapy protocol exemption paragraph (process, not a criterion). No criterion in the document has a duration.

Program exceptions: FEP follows FEP guidelines, SAO follows SAO guidelines, Medicare Advantage products follow LCD L34028; all three listed as excluded_plans. The document applies to all other lines of business.
All eleven codes are covered subject to the pathways; the document tags no code non-covered or investigational. No ICD-10 codes are listed.
